title: Election night surprise on financial sector stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event study with a market model.
- Rationale: The surprise election outcome is a sharp, plausibly exogenous information shock occurring after market close on day 0. Abnormal returns are computed as deviations from expected returns predicted by the market model estimated on a pre-event estimation window.
- Key assumptions:
  - Market efficiency: Prices incorporate the new information when the market opens on day +1; the reaction window is [+1,+3].
  - Correct model for normal returns: The market model estimated on [−10,−2] captures expected returns absent the event.
  - No confounding concurrent firm- or sector-specific events in [+1,+3] that systematically bias abnormal returns.
  - Cross-sectional inference: Tests use cross-sectional variation across stocks; t-tests assume independence across firms after market-model adjustment (acknowledging sector comovement is partially removed by the market factor).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load and analyze event-study data for financial stocks around an election-night surprise

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s15_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))
df <- df[order(df$stock_id, df$event_day), ]

# 2) Estimate firm-level market model on estimation window [-10, -2]
est <- subset(df, event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2)

split_est <- split(est, est$stock_id)
param_list <- lapply(split_est, function(d) {
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = d)
  co <- coef(fit)
  s  <- summary(fit)$sigma
  # Guard against any missing coefficients (edge case)
  alpha_hat <- if ("(Intercept)" %in% names(co)) co["(Intercept)"] else 0
  beta_hat  <- if ("mkt_ret" %in% names(co)) co["mkt_ret"] else 0
  c(alpha_hat = alpha_hat, beta_hat = beta_hat, sigma_hat = s)
})

params <- do.call(rbind, param_list)
params_df <- data.frame(
  stock_id  = as.integer(names(split_est)),
  alpha_hat = params[, "alpha_hat"],
  beta_hat  = params[, "beta_hat"],
  sigma_hat = params[, "sigma_hat"]
)

# 3) Merge parameters back and compute abnormal returns
df <- merge(df, params_df, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
df$AR_ols <- with(df, ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret))

# Robustness 1: Market-adjusted abnormal return (MAR)
df$MAR <- with(df, ret - mkt_ret)

# Robustness 2: Use provided beta with alpha re-estimated conditional on beta (on [-10,-2])
alpha_fix_df <- aggregate(
  (est$ret - est$beta * est$mkt_ret),
  by = list(stock_id = est$stock_id),
  FUN = mean
)
names(alpha_fix_df)[2] <- "alpha_fix"
df <- merge(df, alpha_fix_df, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
df$AR_givenbeta <- with(df, ret - (alpha_fix + beta * mkt_ret))

# Helper to compute cross-sectional CAR and t-tests
car_stats <- function(data, start_day, end_day, ar_col) {
  sub <- subset(data, event_day >= start_day & event_day <= end_day, 
                select = c("stock_id", ar_col))
  # Sum ARs within stock over the window
  car <- aggregate(sub[[ar_col]], by = list(stock_id = sub$stock_id), FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(car)[2] <- "CAR"
  N <- nrow(car)
  mean_car <- mean(car$CAR)
  sd_car   <- sd(car$CAR)
  tval <- mean_car / (sd_car / sqrt(N))
  pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = N - 1)
  pos  <- sum(car$CAR > 0)
  list(N = N, mean_car = mean_car, sd_car = sd_car, t = tval, p = pval, pos = pos)
}

# Primary test: event happened after close on day 0, so use [+1, +3]
res_primary <- car_stats(df, 1, 3, "AR_ols")

# Also report [0, +3] as in the research question
res_0_3 <- car_stats(df, 0, 3, "AR_ols")

# Placebo window: [-3, -1]
res_placebo <- car_stats(df, -3, -1, "AR_ols")

# Robustness: Market-adjusted returns on [+1, +3]
res_mar <- car_stats(df, 1, 3, "MAR")

# Robustness: Provided-beta model on [+1, +3]
res_givenbeta <- car_stats(df, 1, 3, "AR_givenbeta")

# Optional: Average abnormal return by day in [+1,+3] to see concentration
tmp <- subset(df, event_day >= 1 & event_day <= 3)
aar <- aggregate(tmp$AR_ols, by = list(event_day = tmp$event_day), FUN = mean)
names(aar)[2] <- "AAR"

# 4) Print clear numerical results (in percent for interpretability)
to_pct <- function(x) 100 * x

cat("Primary result: Mean CAR in [+1,+3] using OLS market model\n")
cat(sprintf("N=%d, Mean CAR=%.3f%%, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, Positives=%d\n\n",
            res_primary$N, to_pct(res_primary$mean_car), res_primary$t, res_primary$p, res_primary$pos))

cat("Event-window [0,+3] using OLS market model\n")
cat(sprintf("N=%d, Mean CAR=%.3f%%, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, Positives=%d\n\n",
            res_0_3$N, to_pct(res_0_3$mean_car), res_0_3$t, res_0_3$p, res_0_3$pos))

cat("Placebo window [-3,-1] using OLS market model\n")
cat(sprintf("N=%d, Mean CAR=%.3f%%, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, Positives=%d\n\n",
            res_placebo$N, to_pct(res_placebo$mean_car), res_placebo$t, res_placebo$p, res_placebo$pos))

cat("Robustness: Market-adjusted returns (MAR) on [+1,+3]\n")
cat(sprintf("N=%d, Mean CAR=%.3f%%, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, Positives=%d\n\n",
            res_mar$N, to_pct(res_mar$mean_car), res_mar$t, res_mar$p, res_mar$pos))

cat("Robustness: Provided beta with re-estimated alpha on [+1,+3]\n")
cat(sprintf("N=%d, Mean CAR=%.3f%%, t=%.2f, p=%.4f, Positives=%d\n\n",
            res_givenbeta$N, to_pct(res_givenbeta$mean_car), res_givenbeta$t, res_givenbeta$p, res_givenbeta$pos))

cat("Average abnormal returns by day (AAR) in [+1,+3], OLS market model:\n")
print(data.frame(event_day = aar$event_day, AAR_pct = round(to_pct(aar$AAR), 3)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive mean CAR for financials in [+1,+3], reflecting expectations of deregulation and a steeper yield curve after an unexpected election outcome favorable to banks.
- Magnitude: Approximately +2% to +4% over [+1,+3]. AAR likely concentrated on day +1, with smaller follow-through on days +2 and +3. Placebo window should be near zero and insignificant. Robustness using market-adjusted returns and the provided-beta variant should yield similar positive, significant CARs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — political event; market model; focus on [+1,+3] for after-hours announcement
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Financial stocks earned positive abnormal returns after election surprise
